item.title: U.S. allies forge trade deals with each other amid Trump tariffs
item.description:
America's longtime allies are cutting deals among themselves after a year of confrontations with the Trump administration, seeking refuge from the president's unpredictable tariff threats that have upended the global trading order. The flurry of activity comes as central banks dump dollars in favor of gold, and the greenback has slid to its lowest level since 2022.

Last week, the European Union and India announced a landmark free trade agreement after nearly two decades of stalled negotiations, while the EU-Mercosur deal signed last month caps 25 years of talks with South American nations. These agreements represent a pivot by major economies to reduce their dependence on the United States.

item.title: Iranian gunboats order US tanker to halt in Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
Armed Iranian Revolutionary Guard gunboats approached and challenged the US-flagged tanker Stena Imperative in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, ordering the vessel to stop and prepare for boarding before the ship evaded the confrontation and continued on its route, according to British maritime security firm Vanguard Tech.

The incident, which occurred approximately 16 nautical miles north of Oman within the inbound Traffic Separation Scheme, comes just days before scheduled US-Iran talks in Istanbul aimed at defusing tensions over Tehran's nuclear program.

item.title: Russia resumes strikes on Ukraine after Trump-brokered pause expires
item.description:
Russian missiles and drones struck Ukrainian cities overnight on February 2-3, targeting energy infrastructure across multiple regions as a brief Trump-brokered pause expired, leaving hundreds of thousands without heating during the coldest night of the winter.

The attacks hit Kyiv, Kharkiv, Dnipro, Sumy, and Odesa as temperatures plunged to -20°C (-4°F), causing fires and widespread damage just days before a new round of trilateral peace talks scheduled in Abu Dhabi on February 4-5. The resumption of strikes followed an agreement by Russian President Vladimir Putin to halt attacks on Ukrainian cities for a limited period at the personal request of U.S. President Donald Trump, with the Kremlin stating the pause would last only until February 1.

item.title: Giant rock formations deep beneath Earth shape magnetic field, study finds
item.description:
Two continent-sized formations of superhot rock buried nearly 2,900 kilometers beneath Africa and the Pacific Ocean have been quietly influencing Earth's magnetic field for hundreds of millions of years, according to new research that challenges longstanding assumptions about the planet's deep interior.

The study, published this week in Nature Geoscience and led by scientists at the University of Liverpool in collaboration with the University of Leeds, combines ancient magnetic records preserved in rocks with advanced supercomputer simulations to reveal how these massive underground structures affect the liquid iron core that generates Earth's protective magnetic field.

item.title: Poll: 76% of Greenlanders oppose joining the United States
item.description:
A new poll has found that 76% of Greenlanders oppose the idea of their Arctic territory becoming part of the United States, with widespread concerns about trading their Danish welfare system for American healthcare, senior care, and education systems.

The survey, conducted by Danish pollster Sune Steffen Hansen in January 2026, reveals that just 8% of Greenland's residents believe it would be advantageous to join the United States, while 16% remain undecided. According to a separate report in The Wall Street Journal, only 3% of Greenlanders view the benefits provided by the U.S. government as "very positive," while a substantial 59% have a predominantly or strongly negative perception.

item.title: US shoots down Iranian drone approaching aircraft carrier
item.description:
A US F-35C fighter jet shot down an Iranian drone that "aggressively approached" the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier in the Arabian Sea on Tuesday, marking a sharp escalation in maritime tensions between Washington and Tehran just days before planned nuclear negotiations.

The Shahed-139 drone was destroyed as the carrier sailed approximately 500 miles from Iran's southern coast, according to U.S. Central Command. No American personnel were harmed and no equipment was damaged.

item.title: Apple brings AI agents from Anthropic, OpenAI to Xcode
item.description:
Apple on Tuesday announced the release of Xcode 26.3, bringing agentic AI coding capabilities to its flagship development environment through integrations with Anthropic's Claude Agent and OpenAI's Codex. The update allows AI models to autonomously explore projects, write code, run tests, and fix errors within the IDE used by developers building apps for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Watch.

The Xcode 26.3 Release Candidate is available to all Apple Developer Program members today, with a broader App Store release expected soon.

item.title: EU and UK hold London talks on trade, defense cooperation
item.description:
European Union and UK officials opened a fresh push for closer cooperation this week, using meetings in London to accelerate negotiations on easing post-Brexit trade frictions and rebuilding security ties as the 10th anniversary of the 2016 referendum approaches.

The discussions brought together UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves and senior EU figures including Maroš Šefčovič and Valdis Dombrovskis, amid growing agreement on both sides that the current geopolitical and trade environment is pushing Europe and Britain toward more structured collaboration.

item.title: US-backed consortium agrees to buy 40% of Glencore's Congo mines
item.description:
Glencore PLC said it has signed a **non-binding memorandum of understanding** that could see a US-backed investment group acquire **40% of Glencore’s interests** in two major copper-and-cobalt operations in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC): Mutanda Mining (Mumi) and Kamoto Copper Company (KCC). The companies said the talks imply a **combined enterprise value of about $9 billion** for the two assets.

The prospective buyer is the **Orion Critical Mineral Consortium (Orion CMC)**, which Glencore said was established in October 2025 and is led by Orion Resource Partners in partnership with the US government. Glencore shares rose in London trading after the announcement.

item.title: China warns Panama of 'heavy price' after canal port ruling
item.description:
China on Tuesday denounced a Panamanian Supreme Court ruling that struck down the legal basis for a Hong Kong company’s long-running concessions to operate two ports at either end of the Panama Canal, escalating a dispute that has become entangled in U.S.-China rivalry and a major global ports transaction.

In a statement carried by China’s Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office, Beijing described the decision as “absurd,” “shameful and pathetic,” and warned Panama it could face “heavy” political and economic consequences if it pressed ahead—language that signals the case has moved beyond a commercial disagreement into a diplomatic flashpoint.

item.title: US Navy shoots down Iranian drone approaching carrier
item.description:
A US F-35C fighter jet shot down an Iranian drone that "aggressively approached" the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln in the Arabian Sea on Tuesday, marking a direct military encounter between American and Iranian forces just days before high-stakes diplomatic talks are set to begin.

The incident occurred as the Lincoln was transiting approximately 500 miles from Iran's southern coast when an Iranian Shahed-139 drone "unnecessarily maneuvered toward the ship," according to US Central Command spokesman Capt. Tim Hawkins. The drone continued its approach "despite de-escalatory measures taken by US forces operating in international waters," prompting the F-35C to intercept and destroy it in self-defense.

No American service members were injured and no US equipment was damaged during the encounter.

item.title: Markets tumble on AI disruption fears and Bitcoin drops
item.description:
Global equities slid Tuesday as a new wave of investor anxiety hit technology and data-heavy stocks, with concerns that fast-improving “agentic” AI tools could pressure margins and upend business models. Bitcoin also sank to its lowest level since November 2024, adding to a broader “risk-off” tone across markets.

The selloff was catalyzed by fresh attention on AI moving from back-end capabilities into workflow products—most notably a legal-focused tool from Anthropic—prompting investors to reassess which software and information businesses are defensible as automation improves.

item.title: Nvidia CEO says OpenAI deal on track, dismisses drama
item.description:
Nvidia Corp. CEO Jensen Huang said the chipmaker still expects to put money into OpenAI, pushing back on reports that a headline-grabbing plan floated last year had stalled and emphasizing that any investment would unfold in steps rather than as a single, immediate $100 billion check.

In an interview with CNBC, Huang said Nvidia would participate in OpenAI’s next fundraising round and would also be open to investing in an eventual initial public offering, calling the relationship “on track” and dismissing the notion of internal “drama.”

item.title: Starmer, Trump discuss Ukraine as peace talks resume
item.description:
British Prime Minister Keir Starmer spoke with U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday about the deteriorating situation in Ukraine, where overnight Russian strikes left thousands without heat amid freezing temperatures, according to the UK government. The conversation came as Ukrainian negotiators traveled to Abu Dhabi for a second round of trilateral peace discussions scheduled for Wednesday and Thursday.

Russia launched 450 drones and over 60 missiles overnight on February 2-3, targeting energy infrastructure across eight Ukrainian regions, according to Ukraine's Foreign Affairs Minister Andrii Sybiha. The attacks knocked out heating for 1,170 residential buildings in Kyiv as temperatures dropped to -17 Celsius (1.4 Fahrenheit), Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported. The strikes also hit thermal power plants in Kharkiv and Dnipro, leaving at least four people injured.

The assault marked the heaviest attack on Ukraine's energy sector in 2026 and signaled the end of a brief ceasefire on energy targets. Trump had announced on January 29 that Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to pause strikes on energy facilities for a week, but the Kremlin said the pause would only last until February 1.

item.title: UAE and Colossal Biosciences to build genetic 'Noah's Ark' in Dubai
item.description:
The United Arab Emirates and Colossal Biosciences announced a $60 million partnership on Tuesday to create the world's first BioVault, a genetic preservation facility that company leaders describe as a "modern-day Noah's Ark" designed to safeguard endangered species from extinction.

The initiative, unveiled at the World Governments Summit in Dubai, will establish the Colossal BioVault and World Preservation Lab as a permanent feature at Dubai's Museum of the Future, with construction expected to be completed by 2027. The announcement marks one of the largest conservation biotechnology deals between a government and a private company.

item.title: Starmer, Trump agree to work together on Diego Garcia base
item.description:
Prime Minister Keir Starmer and President Donald Trump held discussions on Tuesday regarding the future of the joint UK-US military base on Diego Garcia, marking their first known conversation on the topic since Trump branded the sovereignty deal an "act of great stupidity" last month.

According to Downing Street, the two leaders "recognised its strategic importance" and "agreed their governments would continue working closely to guarantee the future operation of the base and speak again soon."

item.title: CK Hutchison launches arbitration against Panama over port ruling
item.description:
CK Hutchison Holdings announced Wednesday that its Panama Ports Company unit has initiated international arbitration proceedings against the Republic of Panama, following a court ruling last week that annulled its licenses to operate two major ports along the Panama Canal.

Panama's Supreme Court ruled on January 29 that the contracts were unconstitutional, citing exclusive privileges and tax exemptions granted to the Hong Kong-based conglomerate. The decision threatens CK Hutchison's planned $23 billion sale of its global port operations to a consortium led by BlackRock and Mediterranean Shipping Company.

item.title: Trump says Putin 'kept his word' after Russia's largest 2026 attack on Ukraine
item.description:
President Donald Trump defended Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tuesday after Moscow resumed devastating attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, saying Putin "kept his word" on a temporary halt to strikes — despite the pause ending after four days, not the promised week.

"It was Sunday to Sunday, and he opened up and hit them hard last night," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office. "He kept his word on that. One week is a lot — we'll take anything, because it's really cold over there."

The comments came hours after Russia launched what Ukrainian officials described as the largest attack of 2026, deploying more than 450 drones and 70 missiles at energy infrastructure during temperatures below -20°C (-4°F). The assault left over 1,000 residential buildings in Kyiv without heating and caused severe damage to power facilities in Kharkiv.

item.title: US-UK team develops real-time Arctic sea ice prediction model
item.description:
A team of US and UK scientists has developed a new method capable of generating accurate, real-time predictions of Arctic sea ice extent, offering a crucial tool for climate monitoring and Indigenous communities who depend on stable ice conditions for their livelihoods.

The research, published in the journal Chaos by AIP Publishing on February 3, represents a breakthrough in subseasonal forecasting—predicting sea ice conditions from early summer through fall when ice coverage in the Arctic reaches its annual minimum.

item.title: Gold extends rally as US-Iran tensions drive safe-haven demand
item.description:
Gold prices surged over 2% on Wednesday, building on their strongest single-day performance since November 2008, as investors seeking refuge from escalating U.S.-Iran tensions and a weakening dollar piled into the precious metal.

Spot gold climbed 2.2% to $5,044.74 per ounce in early trading Wednesday, according to Reuters, after posting a 5.9% gain on Tuesday that marked the metal's largest daily increase in nearly two decades. The rally follows a turbulent week that saw gold swing wildly from record highs to steep losses and back again.
